kids: Last one in is a seagull!
It is cold! It is cold! I am still in!
Dad, look, a shell with nobody home!
Do not splash my sandwich. The sandwich did nothing.
Race you to the close buoy. Walk. I said walk.
The wave ate my hat. The wave can keep it.
I found a crab. It found me first.
Ice cream is faster than I am. Help.
Mum, the sand is hotter than the kettle.
I am a shark. A small, polite shark.
Count my footprints. There are too many.
The lifeguard waved. I am famous now.
Bucket is full of sea. That was the plan.
Ha! You missed. The water did not.
Can we stay until the lights? Please. Please.
families: Sunscreen, then sea. That is the law of this towel.
Who has the naartjies. Do not say the gulls.
We can see you. Stay this side of the flag.
Shoes in a pile. We will find them. Probably.
Eat first. Swim second. Argue third.
That is far enough. The buoy is not a dare today.
Photo, then you may disappear into the water.
Share the chips or nobody gets chips. Democracy.
The wind is free. The soft serve is not. One each.
Five more minutes. I have said that twice. I mean it now.
lifeguard: Flags are up. Read them. Then you may get brave.
Close buoy only. The far one is a postcard, not a plan.
If I blow the whistle, you come in. Not a debate.
Shoes off the path at night. The sea stays a sound.
You made it back. Drink water. Then you may brag.
